architecture.paradigm: Package-by-feature React (Context Provider) + functional core (marmot-ts / ts-mls) + e2e Playwright fixtures. MarmotProvider owns all MLS state and test-hook registrations. Production code has zero knowledge of e2e. e2e communicates with the browser exclusively through window.__notestrTest* hooks (via page.evaluate) and Playwright DOM locators.

boundary_rules: Production code (src/) never imports from e2e/. The boundary is one-directional.
Test hooks are installed only when isTestRuntime() is true (NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E=1 or NODE_ENV=test). Never installed in production builds.
e2e talks to the browser exclusively through window.__notestrTest* hooks (via page.evaluate) or Playwright DOM locators.
All hooks installed in the same useEffect share one closure over state.groups, state.client, pubkey. Installing a new hook in this block adds no new dependencies.
marmot-ts pure helpers (getGroupMembers, etc.) are importable freely in src/.
seams: Group lookup by idStr: state.groups.find(e => e.idStr === groupId) — pattern at client.tsx:441–450; reused by all three new hooks.
Epoch path: group.state.groupContext.epoch (bigint) → coerce via Number() at hook boundary (AC-HOOK-3).
Property-test data flow: fc.commands → Command.run → two-party.ts helper → page.evaluate(window.__hook) → state.groups → marmot-ts pure helper → serialized return → expect().
A14 data flow: openNdkSubscriber(relays) → subscriber.waitForDuration(filter, 2000) → expect(events.length).toBe(0). Wire-level observation, not MLS-decrypt.

Between fc.commands runs only model.reset() is called — no clearAppState, no relay reset. Cross-run MLS state pollution is real and addressed by scoping.

tooling.typescript: 5.9.3, strict:true, target:ES2022 — bigint assignment to number errors without explicit coercion. ES2022 supports bigint literals natively.
tooling.ts_noUnusedLocals: false — dead openNdkSubscriber import does not error today; AC-A14-5 requires the import to become live, not be removed.
tooling.relay: strfry via dockurr/strfry:latest, tmpfs at /app/strfry-db. No server-side kind/tag filter plugin — #h filtering is REQ-level (NIP-01 standard).
tooling.strfry_tag_filter_assumption: AC-A14-8 documents the wire-level interpretation: the test trusts strfry honours #h tag filtering in REQ responses (standard NIP-01). No write-policy plugin gates kind-445 server-side.
